q-113559.name: Question 1
q-113559.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B$ to the basis $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B$ are given below. What is $[x]_{C}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -6\end{aligned}]
$$
q-113559.worked_solution:
Given the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C,$ we find the coordinates of $x$ relative to $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-37 \\ 28\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-82703.name: Question 2
q-82703.problem:
$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -4 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

 

The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ is given above. Find $[x]_{C}$ given that $x=4{b}_{2}-2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{3}.$
q-82703.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $x=4{b}_{2}-2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{3},$ we have

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Given the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C,$ we find the coordinates of $x$ relative to $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -4 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 10 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-36500.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B$ to the basis $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B$ are given below. What is $[x]_{C}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$
q-36500.worked_solution:
Given the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C,$ we find the coordinates of $x$ relative to $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-22 \\ 21\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ is given above. Find $[x]_{C}$ given that $x=4{b}_{3}-2{b}_{1}.$
q-37152.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $x=4{b}_{3}-2{b}_{1},$ we have

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Given the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C,$ we find the coordinates of $x$ relative to $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 7 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -14 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-82707.name: Question 6
q-82707.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ to $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ is given below. Find $[x]_{B}$ given that $x=5{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}.$

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$
q-82707.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5\cdot 5-2\cdot 10}[\begin{aligned}5 & -10 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -\frac{2}{5} & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $x=5{c}_{1}-{c}_{2},$ we obtain

$$
[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -\frac{2}{5} & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-113597.name: Question 7
q-113597.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ to $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ is given below. Find $[x]_{B}$ given that $x=4{c}_{1}+6{c}_{2}.$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$
q-113597.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\cdot 6-7\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}6 & -7 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -\frac{7}{3} \\ -1 & \frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $x=4{c}_{1}+6{c}_{2},$ we obtain  

$$
[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ to $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ is given below. Find $[x]_{B}$ given that $x=3{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2}.$

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
q-82599.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 3-(-1)\cdot (-5)}[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $x=3{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2},$ we obtain

$$
[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-36503.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $C$ are given below. What is $[x]_{B}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$
q-36503.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5\cdot 2-(-3)\cdot (-3)}[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}22 \\ 35\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{7\cdot 1-(-2)\cdot (-4)}[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 2 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -4 \\ -2 & -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

q-82713.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{S\to B}$ from $S$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to S}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{7\cdot 2-3\cdot 5}[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ 3 & -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ 3 & -7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -8\end{aligned}]},\,[x]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

The basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the standard basis $S$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
q-36488.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 \\ -2 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{S\to B}$ from $S$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to S}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 \\ -2 & -8\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\cdot (-8)-9\cdot (-2)}[\begin{aligned}-8 & -9 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3} & \frac{3}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3} & \frac{3}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}18 & -29 \\ -5 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-11 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$

$$

$$
